answer.question: Can artificial turf count as landscaping in Federal Heights?
answer.answer: Not toward the minimum. City code rules out artificial turf for meeting required landscaping on sites that need a landscape plan, such as new apartments and businesses. A detached house or duplex doesn't need one.

blocks.h2: Turf can't fill the landscaping Federal Heights requires.
blocks.takeaway: City code won't count artificial turf toward the landscaping a site must keep. Where it allows something that isn't alive, the code names decorative rock, not turf.
paras: Federal Heights writes its own zoning code. Section 70-512 lists what landscaping can be made of, from grass, shrubs and trees to xeriscape, bark and rock, then rules out artificial trees, shrubs, turf or plants for meeting the minimum (Federal Heights Municipal Code).

Every part of the site not covered by buildings or parking has to be landscaped, and all of it watered by an automatic underground system with 100 percent coverage. Where the code wants something that isn't alive, it names decorative rock laid 3 inches deep over 10-mil plastic.

blocks.h2: Apartments, businesses and park expansions carry a landscape plan.
blocks.takeaway: The rule reaches sites that need a landscape plan, like a new building, a big addition or an expanded parking lot. Swapping planted beds for turf on one starts with Planning.
paras: The rule bites where a landscape plan is required. Section 70-507 asks for one with a site development plan, and with any parking lot that grows by 10 percent or more. Section 70-468 says who needs a site development plan: a new principal building, an addition or accessory building bigger than 20 percent of the floor area already on the site, or a 20 percent change to an existing mobile home park. Detached single-family homes, two-family homes and a manufactured home set up in an existing park are left out (Federal Heights Municipal Code).

The Planning and Zoning Commission reviews that plan and City Council decides it. The city's Development Review Application, as posted in September 2026, lists landscape plan review on its own at $250 (City of Federal Heights).

An approved plan stays with the land. Section 70-513 makes each property owner keep it watered and replace dead plants with the same type within 180 days, existing development included. Under Section 70-509, a change that takes landscaped area below the minimum, brings in dissimilar materials or alters drainage is reviewed as a new plan, and Section 70-514 lets the city fix lapsed upkeep and bill for it after 30 days' written notice. So swapping planted beds for turf on one of these sites starts with Planning, and our Colorado turf law guide covers the state's separate limits for businesses and shared ground.

blocks.kicker: A house, duplex or manufactured home
blocks.h2: On a house lot, ask about the work around the turf.
blocks.takeaway: A house or duplex lot sits outside the landscape-plan rule, but ask Planning about your full scope. A drop steeper than a foot in 3 feet needs a permitted retaining wall; we measure the fall.
paras: A detached house or a duplex doesn't need a site development plan, so the landscape plan rule doesn't reach it, and the code names artificial turf nowhere else. What the code text doesn't settle is whether re-landscaping a yard needs any city review. Ask Federal Heights Planning, with your address and the full scope, digging, grading and sprinkler changes included, before we draw a layout (City of Federal Heights). Our permit article lists what to bring.

The code does cover the walls that often come with a level lawn or putting green. Any fence or retaining wall needs a building permit and a drawing, and a retaining wall is required wherever the ground drops more than a foot for every 3 feet (Federal Heights Municipal Code). We measure the fall at the free visit, so you know early whether that permit comes before the turf.

If you rent a space in a manufactured-home park, the park runs the ground around your home. The code puts the park's owner or operator in charge of managing it and keeping its facilities in repair (Federal Heights Municipal Code). Ask the park office before you plan a turf patch or dog area.

blocks.h2: Westminster's water, and Westminster's drought stage.
blocks.takeaway: Federal Heights follows Westminster's drought plan, now a voluntary watch asking for no more than 3 watering days a week. Turf needs no watering days and no mowing to stay under the weed-height rule.
paras: Federal Heights buys its water. Its 2026 water quality report says all of it in 2025 was treated surface water bought from Westminster and drawn from Standley Lake, where earlier years had 1 to 3 percent from a city well in the Arapahoe aquifer (City of Federal Heights). The city follows Westminster's drought plan.

That put Federal Heights in a voluntary Drought Watch from 15 April 2026, with Clear Creek Basin snowpack tracking close to 2002, the driest year on record. You're asked to water no more than 3 days a week, before 10 a.m. or after 6 p.m., and mandatory restrictions aren't in place (City of Federal Heights). On 12 September 2026 Westminster's drought page still showed a Drought Watch, with its Standley Lake storage account 95% full (City of Westminster). The mandatory two-day schedule on our Northglenn page isn't yours. Federal Heights Public Works (303-412-3539) has the current stage.

Dry summers meet the weed code as well. Section 30-189 makes it unlawful to let weeds or grass grow past six inches within 100 feet of a building or street, planter strip included (Federal Heights Municipal Code). A turf area needs no watering days and no mowing to stay under that line, though weeds can still work in at the edges.

blocks.h2: Loam on top, heavy clay a few inches down.
blocks.takeaway: Loam sits over heavy clay a few inches down, and water moves far slower through it. We check the ground at the free visit and build the base and fall for that clay.
paras: USDA soil data at two points in the city shows Platner and Renohill loam. Platner's topsoil is about 19% clay, but from about 6 to 20 inches down it is about 40%. Renohill runs 23% at the surface and 45% from about 4 inches. Water moves through those clay layers about ten times slower than through the topsoil, and they rate 7.3 and 7.5 for linear extensibility, a measure of how much a soil swells when wet (USDA).

A turf base sits on or near that layer. We check it at the free visit, prepare the packed ground, build the base for it and set the fall so rain runs off the clay instead of sitting on it. What goes under artificial turf walks through the layers.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Federal Heights, CO?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and commercial turf in Federal Heights, CO. Federal Heights is its own home-rule city, with its own zoning code and water bought from Westminster, so the rules on our Westminster, Northglenn and Thornton pages don't carry over. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can turf go in a manufactured-home park's recreation area?
faq.a: Ask before anyone buys it. Parks in the city's R-4 mobile home district must give 8 percent of the park to recreation and park use, in parcels of at least 2.4 acres (Federal Heights Municipal Code). Whether artificial turf can serve that area, and whether a change there needs review, are questions for Federal Heights Planning.

faq.q: Which Federal Heights office answers which question?
faq.a: Planning handles zoning questions, landscape plans and development review (City of Federal Heights). The Building Department takes permit applications, a fence or retaining wall included, and books inspections on 303-412-3534 (City of Federal Heights).
